summary:
Scope note: the computed task asked for desert gazebo spa research (topic spa_build). The user's relayed request asked for something else: where to get the RV trailer, what it could look like, and used and new budgets. The harness says the user's request wins where the two conflict, so this covers the RV trailer. No spa research was done. The web search budget ran out near the end, so a few gaps remain (insurance, loan rates, exact A/C specs).

KEY RULES: San Bernardino County lets you live in an RV or travel trailer while you build your own house, under a Temporary Structure Permit. Your house building permit has to be issued first. Moving the trailer onto the lot before then can bring penalties. The permit lasts 12 months, renews 12 months at a time, and caps at 5 years. You need a current California DMV registration for the unit. If the trailer is self-contained, you also need a sewage pumping contract. If the lot is inside the Town of Yucca Valley, the town's own code applies instead: self-contained RVs, one year plus one-year extensions, 4 years total, and the permit ends when the house is done. So buy something DMV-registrable, a travel trailer or fifth wheel. Avoid a park model unless the county approves it first.

WHERE TO BUY (closest first): Blue Compass RV Palm Desert, Mike Thompson's RV (Cathedral City and Colton), Camping World Colton, I-15 RV and used lots in Hesperia/Victorville, and Airstream Inland Empire in Temecula. Farther out: Airstream Los Angeles (San Gabriel) and Airstream of San Diego (San Marcos). Lance builds its trailers in Lancaster, a high-desert town, and runs factory tours; you buy through dealers. Happier Camper has an LA showroom. Used listings: Airstream Marketplace, RV Trader, Autotrader RV, RVUSA, RV Universe. The California RV Supershow in Pomona runs March 19-21, 2027.

NEW PRICES:
- Airstream 2027 "from" prices: World Traveler $64,400, Basecamp $69,900, Bambi $75,400, Caravel $92,400, Flying Cloud $115,900, Globetrotter $147,400.
- Northwood Arctic Fox NXT 22GT (built for four seasons): $46,995-$55,495 on sale, against MSRPs around $67k-$72k.
- Outdoors RV Creek Side and Timber Ridge: about $50k-$87k.
- Lance 1985: MSRP about $75k-$88k.
- Oliver Legacy Elite II: about $80k-$85k.
- Happier Camper: $39,950-$74,950.
- Bowlus: $150k-$185k.

USED PRICES:
- Used Airstream Flying Cloud: $23,800-$106,000, average $72,833.
- 2016 Flying Cloud 25: $52,998. 2019 Flying Cloud 23FB: $58,849.
- 2023 Arctic Fox 25Y in Kerman, CA: $48,900.
- Renovated 1970s 31-ft Airstream Sovereigns: about $32k-$55k asking. Unrenovated or project shells: $9.5k-$25k.
- Entry-level used trailers in Palm Desert: about $13k-$18k.

RESALE: A 2026 study of five-year-old trailers found Airstreams kept about 76.6% of MSRP, against 46.7% for the weakest brands. That favors buying a used Airstream (or a strong four-season brand) and selling it once the house is done. Renting long-term runs an estimated $3k-$6k a month, which is usually worse than buying and reselling.

DESERT FIT: RV air conditioners pull the inside only about 20F below outside, so in 100F+ heat use shade, a 50A/two-A/C rig and a white or silver exterior. In winter use skirting plus a heater, because nights freeze.

LOOK: a silver-shelled trailer under a white steel carport, with coral-red lattice (changsal) screens, blush and peach linens and black hardware. It suits her high-key black-and-white photography.

BUDGETS (all-in estimates, before septic, well or utility-line work):
- Lean (used trailer): about $17k-$43k.
- Balanced (new Arctic Fox / Basecamp or a used Flying Cloud, plus carport): about $61k-$88k.
- Premium (new Flying Cloud / Oliver / Globetrotter, top carport and finishes): about $106k-$198k.

findings.title: County permit for living in an RV or travel trailer while building
findings.detail:
San Bernardino County EZOP Temporary Structure Permit checklist (Rev. 6/2025, citing Development Code Title 8 Div. 4):
- What it covers: 'A recreational vehicle or travel trailer occupied as residential quarters on a temporary basis by an individual constructing a residence.' The house building permit must be issued before this permit is approved.
- Placement: the trailer may not go on the lot until the companion building permit is issued and this permit is approved; placing it early 'may result in Penalty Fees and Enforcement Action.'
- Final inspection covers the electrical hookup, gas lines and sewer/water connections. Any Fire District, Environmental Health or Public Works approvals must come first.
- Term: 12 months, renewable for 12 months at a time, never more than 5 years from first issuance. The permit expires if no inspection is called within 180 days.
- Submittals: site/plot plan; current California DMV registration for the unit; a sewage pumping contract if the unit is self-contained; will-serve letters from water and sewer providers if applicable.
- Fees: per the county Master Fee Schedule (amount not found).
- The county FAQ confirms the house permit must already be issued and lists Land Use Services at 909.387.8311.

findings.title: If the lot is inside the Town of Yucca Valley, the town's rules apply instead
findings.detail:
Yucca Valley Zoning Code Section 9.39.050(A) allows 'manufactured homes and self-contained recreational vehicles' (travel trailers are not named) as temporary quarters while the first permanent dwelling is built.
- It can be approved once construction permits are issued.
- Term: one year with one-year extensions, at most 4 years in total.
- It becomes invalid when the building permit is cancelled or construction is complete.
- Section 9.39.060 lets the director require removal and site-restoration measures plus performance security. The permit must be displayed where it can be seen from outside.
- Living in a vehicle is otherwise prohibited.
In short: confirm whether the parcel is incorporated, choose a fully self-contained unit, and plan to sell or store it when the house is finished. The code text comes from a third-party host (gocodebook), so verify it with town planning.

findings.title: Buy a DMV-registered travel trailer or fifth wheel, not a park model
findings.detail:
The county wants a current California DMV registration copy for an RV or trailer, so a normal travel trailer or fifth wheel is the simplest route.
- California law defines a park trailer as up to 400 sq ft and up to 14 ft wide, movable on highways only with a permit.
- The DMV manual says park trailers carry ANSI A119.5 labels and are DMV-titled. Any unit with a HUD data plate gets referred to HCD (state housing). That adds steps and may not count as an 'RV or travel trailer' under the county permit.
- Towing: a regular Class C license covers a trailer coach up to 10,000 lb GVWR. A fifth wheel of 10,000-15,000 lb needs a recreational fifth-wheel endorsement. Heavier trailers need a noncommercial Class A license. (The CHP document is a 2013 revision; verify.)

findings.title: Where to buy near Yucca Valley: multi-brand dealers
findings.detail:
- Blue Compass RV Palm Desert, 77840 Varner Rd, Palm Desert 92211 (formerly Holland RV). Has carried Jayco, Grand Design, Forest River, Alliance, Brinkley and Keystone. About 86 new and 26 used units listed; one entry-level travel trailer was listed at $12,899-$17,690.
- Camping World of Colton, 1175 S Mount Vernon Ave. About 127 travel trailer listings, new and used.
- Mike Thompson's RV: Colton, Cathedral City, Santa Fe Springs and Fountain Valley (per press releases).
- Hesperia/Victorville/Apple Valley: I-15 RV in Hesperia (new and used, consignment) and used lots such as Pop RVs and National Vehicle.
- Lance builds in the high desert at 43014 Exchange Place, Lancaster. The factory offers tours, but sales go through dealers.
- Happier Camper has a Los Angeles showroom.
Addresses and stock come from dealer pages and aggregators; confirm before visiting.

findings.title: Where to buy an Airstream in Southern California
findings.detail:
- Airstream Inland Empire, 27969 Jefferson Ave, Temecula 92590 (from a Bank of America dealer directory). About 1.5-2 hours from Yucca Valley.
- Airstream Los Angeles, 1212 E Las Tunas Dr, San Gabriel. Part of Airstream SoCal (Westminster, Midway City, Temecula, Las Vegas).
- Airstream of San Diego, San Marcos (Blue Compass), opened July 17, 2024.
- We Are Airstream announced a Ventura store.
Used Airstreams are also sold on airstreammarketplace.com. Example: a 2024 25-ft International in Temecula asking $120,000. airstream.com shows a $1,000 Airstream Supply Co. gift card for Basecamp purchases July 1-Oct 31, 2026, which ends a week from today. Check Airstream's dealer locator before driving.

findings.title: New Airstream prices (2027 model-year cards on airstream.com)
findings.detail:
Airstream 'from' prices on airstream.com:
- World Traveler $64,400: 2027, 17-22 ft, single axle, sleeps 4, 2 floor plans.
- Basecamp $69,900: 20 ft, sleeps up to 4, GVWR 4,300-4,500 lb, hitch 508-535 lb, 23 gal fresh water.
- Bambi $75,400.
- Basecamp Xe $88,900.
- Caravel $92,400: 16, 20 or 22 ft, single axle, sleeps 5.
- Flying Cloud $115,900: 23-30 ft, 2 axles, 5 plans, sleeps 8.
- International $128,900. Trade Wind $134,400. Globetrotter $147,400. Classic $195,400.
Dealer examples:
- 2026 Basecamp 16X: MSRP $62,650, sale $57,495 (8% off).
- 2026 Basecamp 20X: MSRPs $74,450-$88,250, sales about $63k-$77k.
- 2026 Flying Cloud 25FB: about $110k-$137k at dealers.
- JD Power lists the 2026 Caravel 22FB at $90,300 and the Flying Cloud 25FB Queen at $121,900.

findings.title: Four-season trailers (better insulated for heat and cold): Northwood, Outdoors RV, Lance, Oliver
findings.detail:
- Northwood (La Grande, OR) calls itself a 'true 4-season' maker. Its Arctic Fox Edge lists high-density block foam, heated holding tanks, thermal-pane windows and an insulated roof.
- 2026 Arctic Fox NXT 22GT (about 24 ft): $46,995-$55,495 on sale against MSRPs of $66,723-$71,569. Bish's Fairfield, CA has one at $49,995 (MSRP $71,212).
- Arctic Fox Edge 22GT: $64,911 (MSRP $84,536).
- Arctic Fox NXT 27SX (31 ft), Fairfield, CA: $66,995 (MSRP $87,779). Edge 27SX: $79,990 (MSRP $109,719).
- Outdoors RV 2026: Creek Side 17RBS MSRP about $59.9k, sale about $52.7k. Creek Side Titanium 19MKS $49,995. Timber Ridge 22MKS/24BKS MSRP about $63k-$64k; 25RDS about $75.8k; Titanium 28RES $86,902.
- Lance: floor lengths 14'10" to 25'6", dry weights 2,905-6,400 lb (the 1985 is 18'9", 4,480 lb). Dual-pane windows, heated enclosed underbelly, block foam with Azdel walls. Lance 1985 MSRPs $74,761-$87,760 (2024-25 listings).
- Oliver: Legacy Elite II (24 ft, GVWR 7,000 lb, double-hull fiberglass, sleeps 3) about $79,995 for 2026 and $85,000 standard for 2027. Legacy Elite (18'5", 3,700 lb dry) 2026 slots are sold out.
These prices come from dealer listings and vary.

findings.title: Design-led options: Happier Camper and Bowlus
findings.detail:
- Happier Camper (LA showroom), 2027 prices: HC1 $39,950; HC1 Venture $44,950; HC1 Studio $54,950 (kitchenette, shower, toilet); Traveler $74,950.
- The HC1 is lightweight fiberglass with a modular cube interior.
- Used: a 2022 HC1 Classic was $19,500 and 2024 Studios were $35k-$39k. One buyer reported about a 1-year build wait.
- Very small for two people living full time. Better afterward as a guest room or photo studio.
- Bowlus: Endless Highways from $185,000 (4,000-4,400 lb), Rivet from $150,000. The Terra Firma is no longer built.

findings.title: Used-market price points
findings.detail:
- Used Airstream Flying Cloud on Autotrader: $23,800-$106,000, average $72,833.
- Examples: 2016 Flying Cloud 25 at $52,998 (Camper's Inn); 2019 Flying Cloud 23FB at $58,849 (Camping World); 2025 25FB at $90,000 private and $95,995 dealer.
- 2023 Arctic Fox 25Y (30 ft) at a Kerman, CA dealer: $48,900.
- 1970s 31-ft Airstream Sovereign/Land Yacht asks: renovated $32k-$54.9k; original or project units $9.5k-$25k. These are asking prices, not sold prices.
- High-desert used lots are mostly fifth wheels and toy haulers, which need a pickup with a fifth-wheel hitch: 2021 Grand Design Solitude $48,000; 2018 Keystone Montana $39,900; 2022 Alliance Valor $67,499.
- Entry-level used travel trailers in Palm Desert were about $13k-$18k.

findings.title: Resale: buy something that holds its value, then sell it when the house is done
findings.detail:
The 2026 RVBlogger study (74 five-year-old trailers, 22 brands and product lines) found 46.7%-76.6% of original MSRP retained. Airstream was best at 76.6% and nuCamp T@B second at 64.4%. Rules of thumb elsewhere put the first-year drop at 20-30%. For a 1-3 year stay, a lightly used Airstream or a strong four-season brand bought and resold usually beats both new budget trailers and renting.
Renting: travel trailers rent for about $100-$200 a day, with 10-20% monthly discounts. That is an estimated $3k-$6k a month, or $36k-$144k over 12-24 months.

findings.title: Desert heat, dust, freeze and power
findings.detail:
- Arizona owners report RV A/C units cool only about 20F below outside temperature (110F outside gives about 90F inside). One A/C struggles above 100F on larger rigs; owners advise two A/Cs on trailers over about 30 ft (anecdotal).
- Shade can feel about 20F cooler. Shade cloth on the sun side cuts inside temps by 5-8F.
- Clean A/C filters weekly in dust. Reflective foil on dual-pane windows may break their seals.
- Power: 30A service is about 3,600 W (120 V x 30 A). 50A service is two 120 V legs, about 12,000 W, which is the practical way to run two A/Cs.
- Winter: EZ Snap no-drill skirting $899.99-$2,099.99 plus Xtreme Heaters 800 W $469 or 1000 W $539. AirSkirts inflatable $1,899-$3,199.

findings.title: Site setup costs: shade structure, power pedestal, delivery, inspection, tax
findings.detail:
- Carport: an 18x36 steel RV cover runs $6,480-$19,440 installed (AA Metal Buildings, 2026 ranges; open-sided, level ground; excludes grading, concrete and permits). Carport Central's 18x46x12 RV cover starts at $7,035. An Arrow 14x38x14 retail kit is rated 100 mph wind / 35 psf snow. Get a stamped wind certification for your ZIP code.
- Power pedestal: a 50/30/20A direct-burial GFCI pedestal is about $415. Electrician labor is about $500 and up per forums; trenching distance drives cost.
- Delivery if you don't tow: travel trailer transport is about $1.50-$3.50 per mile, local moves $150-$300 (guide last updated 2023).
- Used-unit inspection: NRVIA pre-purchase inspection typically $300-$800, up to about $1,200.
- Sales tax: Yucca Valley city rate is 8.75% (6% state, 0.25% county, 1% town, 1.5% special). Unincorporated addresses may differ; check CDTFA's address lookup.

findings.title: Shopping calendar
findings.detail:
- It is the end of the model year: 2027s are on airstream.com and dealers are discounting leftover 2026 stock (Arctic Fox about $16k-$22k under MSRP; Basecamp 16X about 8% off).
- The California RV Supershow in Pomona runs March 19-21, 2027, and is useful for walking through many floor plans in one day.
- An Overland Adventure show is at Fairplex Oct 24-25, 2026.

findings.title: Gaps: not researched (search budget exhausted)
findings.detail:
Not covered:
- Full-timer RV insurance cost.
- 2026 RV loan rates.
- Exact A/C BTU and second-A/C prep for each model.
- DMV registration and vehicle license fee amounts. From background knowledge only, not verified here: the fee is about 0.65% of depreciated value.
- The county permit fee amount.
- Septic or pumping-contract costs in Morongo Basin.
Verify these before finalizing budgets.

risks.risk: Moving the trailer onto the lot (or living in it) before the house building permit and the Temporary Structure Permit are issued
risks.mitigation: Pull the house permit first, then apply for the Temporary Structure Permit through EZOP with the site plan, DMV registration, pumping contract and will-serve letters. Deliver the trailer only after approval.

risks.risk: Not knowing whether the parcel is in the Town of Yucca Valley or unincorporated county (different code, 4-year vs 5-year cap, different tax rate)
risks.mitigation: Look up the parcel's jurisdiction on the county parcel map and confirm with Yucca Valley planning or county Land Use Services before buying

risks.risk: Buying a unit that cannot get California DMV registration (park model, HUD-labeled unit, missing title or out-of-state paperwork)
risks.mitigation: Buy a titled travel trailer or fifth wheel. Check the VIN, title and lien status, and register it before applying for the permit.

risks.risk: Summer heat overwhelms a single A/C, and UV and heat damage cheap trailers (roof seams, delamination)
risks.mitigation: Choose a four-season or aluminum/fiberglass shell with 50A and two A/Cs. Park under a carport or shade cloth with a light-colored roof, and clean filters weekly.

risks.risk: Freezing winter nights split pipes and tanks
risks.mitigation: Heated, enclosed underbelly; skirting plus an under-trailer heater; heated hose; insulate the water line where it leaves the ground

risks.risk: Spring winds tear awnings and rock the trailer; dust gets into seals and A/C
risks.mitigation: Retract awnings when you leave and in wind. Use stabilizers and chocks, and add ground anchors or tie-downs if the installer recommends them. Put the hitch end into the prevailing wind, add lattice or windbreak screens, and gravel the pad.

risks.risk: Hidden water damage or scams in used private sales
risks.mitigation: NRVIA inspection ($300-$800), meet at a dealer or bank, verify the title, never wire a deposit for an unseen unit

risks.risk: Dark exterior wrap (black brand color) adds solar heat
risks.mitigation: Keep the body silver or white. Use black and coral only as thin linework or bands, and keep the roof white.

risks.risk: Lead times for new builds (Oliver 2026 slots full; Happier Camper owners report about 1-year waits)
risks.mitigation: Buy dealer stock or leftover 2026 units now, or buy used

risks.risk: Depreciation, and having to vacate when the house is finished
risks.mitigation: Pick a brand that holds value (Airstream retained 76.6% at 5 years) and plan the sale or storage before final inspection of the house

risks.risk: Tow vehicle mismatch (fifth wheels and 6,000-9,000+ lb trailers need a full-size truck; heavy trailers need a license upgrade)
risks.mitigation: Have it delivered ($1.50-$3.50/mile) since it will sit for 1-3 years, or choose a trailer under 10,000 lb GVWR

next_actions: Confirm the parcel's jurisdiction (Town of Yucca Valley or unincorporated county). Call county Land Use Services (909.387.8311) to get the Temporary Structure Permit fee and ask whether a pumping contract is enough or a septic hookup is required.
Decide tow vs. deliver. If delivering, get 2-3 transporter quotes.
Shortlist and walk through: Arctic Fox NXT 22GT, Lance 1985/2075, Outdoors RV Creek Side, Airstream Basecamp 20X / World Traveler, and a used Flying Cloud 23-25.

design_ideas: 'Silver and coral' concept: a polished Airstream (Basecamp, Flying Cloud or a renovated Sovereign). The aluminum reads as bright white in high-key black-and-white photos and reflects the sun.
Coral-red (#ec4639) changsal / key-fret lattice panels on the trailer, either removable laser-cut window screens or an entry-door privacy screen. They cast lattice shadows inside and outdoors.

Interior palette: matte-white or pale-wood cabinets, black hardware and faucets, blush (#f2d1d1) and peach (#fec6b4) linen bedding and cushions. Replace dated valances with hanji-style (Korean paper) roller shades for soft diffused light.
For a boxy four-season trailer (Arctic Fox, Lance), use a white or silver body with one thin black or coral key-fret band, not a full black wrap, to limit heat.

Park under a white steel carport (18x36, or 18x46 for 30 ft). Add coral lattice screen walls on the west/southwest wind side; they double as a backdrop for brand shoots and become the house carport or workshop later.
Put the door side facing the house build site, with a gravel pad, a simple wood deck with steps, and an outdoor kitchen/table under the carport overhang.
Lean version: a vintage Airstream project shell rebuilt in her black/white/coral style, a content series in itself, and a strong resale story afterward.
After the house is done, a small Happier Camper or Basecamp could become a guest room or photo studio. Check whether the code allows that; temporary occupancy ends at completion.
